reviewed_by: worker-6 source-reviewed adjudication of worker-5 mechanism layer
extraction_scope: Mechanism claims are bounded to source-supported CDK4/cyclin-D interface binding, cellular pRb/proliferation context, and combination in vivo efficacy; no antimicrobial membrane/nucleic-acid mechanism is claimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P2short/P2shortA are CDK4 C-helix-derived hydrocarbon-stapled peptides designed to target the CDK4/cyclin D interface.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Design/sequence/structure context, not standalone activity evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P2short binds cyclins and affects CDK4/cyclin-D ATP-binding context in direct biochemical assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding is not cyclin-D1 exclusive; the paper reports similar binding to multiple cyclins.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P2short internalizes into A549 cells, partially colocalizes with CDK4/cyclin D1, reduces p107Rb phosphorylation, and inhibits NSCLC proliferation.

source_locator.locator: pdf_text:Figure 4 and Figure 5 result sections; xml:fig=4; xml:fig=5

mechanism_claims.limitations: Cellular mechanism is consistent with CDK4 pathway modulation but does not establish antimicrobial activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In the H358 orthotopic mouse model, P2shortA shows antitumor efficacy only when co-administered with Abemaciclib under the tested intrapulmonary regimen.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Peptide-alone activity is not promoted; pulmonary toxicity remains not formally assessed beyond the paper tolerability observations.

caution_findings.finding: The source supports anticancer CDK/cyclin biology, not antimicrobial membrane or nucleic-acid mechanism.
P2shortA alone was insufficient in the reported H358 orthotopic design.
